item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is pretty weak. The ending is a failure; the agents should have been at least as willing to assume the puzzle was just trying to scare them as they were that it was warning them. Moreover, having been "warned", they ought to have been able to protect themselves effectively against a mere knife without having to resort to murder. The Foundation wouldn't have written it up like that anyway; it conveys something like "Obviously we all understand what REALLY happened, but we're willing to brush it under the rug" when, in fact, what happened didn't even make sense, and therefore could not possibly be obvious.

Also, yeah, the puzzle image described could not have shown one guy stabbing an entire group in a single scene. That is bad writing.

This entry should not be here in its current state. If the voting system establishes that it's a good enough entry to keep, then the voting system is broken.

"now defunct Mobile Task Force ███████-12"

Not a terribly huge issue, but why is that black-boxed? I just don't see the need for it. If someone can explain some sort of reasoning for it, great. Not something I'd downvote over, though.

And I'm in agreement on the knife thing. Why is it even mentioned that it's the "standard-issue" knife (let alone the titanium thing)? At the very least, take out "supplied to every Agent" since it's redundant. But really, the sentence should probably read, "… stabbing several other members of the Task Force with a standard-issue combat knife" or something. If he was using a lightsaber, it would be worth mentioning what the stabbing was happening with. Otherwise, a knife is a knife is a knife, right?
